threats.name: Phishing
threats.definition: A social engineering attack that uses deceptive messages or websites to trick people into sharing sensitive information.
threats.howItWorks: An attacker impersonates a trusted sender and directs a target to a fraudulent login page, malicious attachment, or other deceptive request.

threats.name: Malware
threats.definition: Software intentionally designed to disrupt systems, steal information, or gain unauthorized access.
threats.howItWorks: Malware can reach a device through malicious downloads, compromised software, or infected attachments and then execute unwanted actions.

threats.name: Ransomware
threats.definition: A type of malware that encrypts data or otherwise blocks access and demands payment.
threats.howItWorks: After compromising a system, ransomware may encrypt files and display a ransom demand. Some groups also steal data to pressure victims.

threats.name: DDoS Attack
threats.definition: A distributed denial-of-service attack attempts to make a service unavailable by overwhelming it with traffic or requests.
threats.howItWorks: Many devices or sources send traffic toward the same service, exhausting network capacity or server resources.

threats.name: Social Engineering
threats.definition: The manipulation of people into taking actions or revealing information that compromises security.
threats.howItWorks: Attackers exploit trust, urgency, authority, or curiosity to persuade targets to bypass normal security precautions.
